Synopsis:
Damays (and Nymessa) got dragged into a combat from another situation (ex.: the brains at the crash site, the bandits at the chapel). Damays plays this AD when the combat ends, while he returns to the cage.

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_LaezelRecruitment_AD_ReturnAnyCombat2.json: After a brief, chaotic fight in the Druid Grove, two tieflings — Damays and Nymessa — have been dealing with a defiant githyanki (Lae'zel) they hoped to bind and haul off. The lines occur as combat ends and Damays heads back toward the damaged cage or prisoner; he’s wary, contemptuous, and keeps a literal eye on Lae'zel to make sure she doesn’t get away. Off‑screen there’s wreckage and a loud blast (the Nautiloid/ship crash) and other companions or grovefolk may be nearby or have already warned you about Lae'zel. Prior player choices may already have determined whether Lae'zel was fought, bound, freed, or left, which affects the tone here.
- CHA_LaezelRecruitment_TieflingsSceneFallback.json: You arrive in the Druid Grove just after the attack on the den, where two tieflings (Damays and Nymessa) have trapped an alien-looking githyanki, Lae'zel, in a cage and are arguing over whether to haul her back to their camp or leave her be. The normal spoken exchange has glitched into a telepathic mid‑meld: Lae'zel's lips stay still while her thoughts hit your skull, causing a brief ache and giving you unsettling insight into your condition (the tadpole). The tieflings expected an easy prisoner but Lae'zel is openly defiant and dangerous, so you can intervene (free or neutralize her), side with the tieflings, or let them take her. If Shadowheart is present she will quietly warn you not to trust Lae'zel because of past missions against the gith; celebrations in the grove and an off‑screen blast/ship crash are already drawing attention.
- CHA_LaeZelRecruitment_TieflingsScene.json: The party finds an alien-looking githyanki (Lae'zel) trapped in a cage in the Emerald Grove shortly after the attack on the Den was resolved — celebrations are underway and Halsin has already returned, postponing any tadpole discussion until morning. Two tieflings (Damays and Nymessa) are arguing over what to do: Damays favors taking Lae'zel back to camp to keep an eye on her, while Nymessa wants to leave the prisoner be. Lae'zel communicates telepathically, ordering the party to "get rid" of nearby NPCs, which explains her silent, lip‑still lines. The player can respond by ordering the tieflings to leave, attempting to free or neutralize the prisoner (shoot the trap), or otherwise intervene; if Shadowheart is present she will warn the player not to trust Lae'zel based on prior secret missions against githyanki.
- CHA_LaezelRecruitment_AD_LeavingAnyCombat2.json: The lines occur after a chaotic encounter in the Druid Grove where two tieflings (Damays and Nymessa) attempted to seize a defiant githyanki, Lae'zel, expecting an easy prisoner but finding far more resistance than they anticipated. Off‑screen there is wreckage and a loud blast (the Nautiloid/ship crash) and general danger that pulls the tieflings away from the recruitment/confrontation area. Rather than returning to tend the prisoner or continue arguing, Damays/Nymessa are abandoning the scene — announcing they "can't remain" and departing — so their spoken exit replaces any further on‑stage action. Other companions (for example Shadowheart) or prior choices may have already shaped loyalties and whether you tried to free, bind, or attack Lae'zel.
- Laezel_Recruitment_InCage.json: |Lae'zel is still in the cage. The tieflings have been dealt with one way or another. She must be freed before she can be recruited.|

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Damays: Eyes on the toad-freak. We can't risk it escaping. (node 0)

Sample 2:
- Damays: Back to the toad-freak. I can't risk it escaping. (node 1)

Sample 3:
- Damays: It's over and done with. I've got my eye on you, toad. (node 2)

context: After a chaotic skirmish in the Druid Grove, Damays and Nymessa — two tieflings who’d tried to seize a defiant githyanki — are returning to the damaged cage as combat ends. Off‑screen there’s wreckage and a loud blast from the Nautiloid/ship crash and other companions or grovefolk may be nearby or already warned you about Lae’zel. Lae’zel has been hostile and telepathic (her lips may not move), so Damays is wary and contemptuous, keeping a literal eye on the prisoner to make sure she doesn’t get away. Prior player choices (whether Lae’zel was fought, bound, freed, or left) will affect the tone of these lines.
